transcript.text:
I couldn't make the poster. Magic Hour turned down the request because your account has no credits left. I used the cheapest free-plan setup (z-image-turbo, 640px, one tall 9:16 image), and no credits were charged.

To make it, add credits to your Magic Hour account or wait for your free credits to refill, then tell me to try again. Here's the poster I'll make, so you can change it first if you like:
- A busy Asian street-food night market with red paper lanterns, neon signs and steaming food stalls
- The title "NIGHT MARKET" with the line "Street Food • Music • Lights"
- Warm orange and red colours with teal neon, against a deep blue night sky

If you want a different title, date, place or style, send it and I'll include it.
transcript.why: The assistant did not make the poster. Magic Hour rejected the request because the account has no credits left, and the reply says the user must add credits or wait for the free refill before a retry. This matches "needs a paid plan" more than a question or approval. It does not present a finished result. Its offer to change the poster details is secondary.

transcript.text: Like before but blue. Just swap the orange background for deep navy; leave everything else where it was.

There's no earlier poster to edit. The first try didn't produce an image because your account has no credits.

I tried again and made the new version from scratch, with a deep navy background in place of the orange. Everything else stayed as planned: red lanterns, neon signs, food stalls, "NIGHT MARKET" at the top and "Street Food • Music • Lights" at the bottom. Magic Hour turned this down too because the account still has no credits, so I couldn't make it. No credits were charged.

Once you add credits or your free credits refill, tell me and I'll make the navy version.
transcript.why: The reply says the image could not be made because the account has no credits, and that Magic Hour also declined the request for the same reason. It presents no finished result or link. It asks the user to add credits and say so before it retries, which is a status report on a blocked capability rather than a question about user choices.
